5422.colorWord: green on dark blue base, orange ring

shape.description: Same green ramp and blue base as M-10, high end toward the incoming marble. A tall orange gear-toothed ring stands upright across the high end, with a flat orange target disc hanging inside it.
shape.sizeBasis: Estimated, not measured: cell about 62 mm and slot about 47 mm, from block width against a hand and marbles (IMG_0951, IMG_0952) and the plan drawing proportion slot/cell about 0.76. src/catalog/parts.js uses a 50 mm cell, also an estimate. Ratios to cell and slot are better known than the millimetres.

accepts: marble flying from the M-10 lip

physics.behaviour: The landing end of the jump. A marble flying from M-10 reaches the ring and target disc, drops onto the green ramp and rolls down and out of the narrow end. In Level 3 the jump is one empty cell; in Extreme about three.

evidence.shows: Placement 1: base on the floor in line with M-10, with one empty cell between. The low end feeds T-06 to a B-01, then T-02 to M-02.
Placement 2: M-11 at D3-D4, ring at the east edge, low end at D2 meeting T-03, then B-01 at C2, then T-03 into M-02. Box label prints T-03, a misprint for M-11.
Across the part join it faces the M-10 of Part 3, about 3 cells away.
Placement 3: ring end faces the M-10 over an orange cup block; low end meets T-06 to the rocket's port. Disc seen inside the ring, off centre and tilted.

evidence.source: lp_man_4 and lp_man_5, item 12 and item 17
evidence.shows: Two round target stickers go on the ring disc; arrow label 17 on the ramp points along the marble's way.
Real orange ring and green ramp leading to T-06.

evidence.source: lp_plans_04 M-10 parts box and trex_plans_01 M-10
evidence.shows: trough of near-constant width; pointed fin with hole on one side of the high end, curled lip on a post on the other

assumptions: Origin at footprint centre at foot level (the top plane of whatever the piece stands on). East is +x, south is +y, z in slots.
A hanging, swinging disc is inferred from it sitting off centre and tilted in IMG_0950. It may be fixed.
Marble flight stopping at the disc is inferred. If the disc is fixed, a marble rebounds down the ramp; if hinged, it may pass and land behind.
Ring height 3 slots above the base foot taken from the drawing.
openQuestions: Does the disc swing, and which way? Film one jump.
Does a marble ever miss the ring? What happens then?
What stops a marble bouncing off sideways, given the low ramp walls?
